requestBodyFields.name: config-source
requestBodyFields.description: Indicates if this is a locally or remotely configured tunnel. If `local`, manage the tunnel using a YAML file on the origin machine. If `cloudflare`, manage the tunnel on the Zero Trust dashboard.

requestBodyFields.name: name
requestBodyFields.description: A user-friendly name for a tunnel.

requestBodyFields.name: tunnel-secret
requestBodyFields.description: Sets the password required to run a locally-managed tunnel. Must be at least 32 bytes and encoded as a base64 string.

requestBodyFields.name: name
requestBodyFields.description: A user-friendly name for a tunnel.

requestBodyFields.name: tunnel-secret
requestBodyFields.description: Sets the password required to run a locally-managed tunnel. Must be at least 32 bytes and encoded as a base64 string.

requestBodyFields.name: tunnel-config-ingress
requestBodyFields.description: List of public hostname definitions. At least one ingress rule needs to be defined for the tunnel. Provide as a JSON array of objects or @path/to/file.json.

requestBodyFields.name: tunnel-config-origin-request-access-aud-tag
requestBodyFields.description: Access applications that are allowed to reach this hostname for this Tunnel. Audience tags can be identified in the dashboard or via the List Access policies API.

requestBodyFields.name: tunnel-config-origin-request-access-required
requestBodyFields.description: Deny traffic that has not fulfilled Access authorization.

requestBodyFields.name: tunnel-config-origin-request-access-team-name
requestBodyFields.description: The config.originRequest.access.teamName field

requestBodyFields.name: tunnel-config-origin-request-ca-pool
requestBodyFields.description: Path to the certificate authority (CA) for the certificate of your origin. This option should be used only if your certificate is not signed by Cloudflare.

requestBodyFields.name: tunnel-config-origin-request-connect-timeout
requestBodyFields.description: Timeout for establishing a new TCP connection to your origin server. This excludes the time taken to establish TLS, which is controlled by tlsTimeout.

requestBodyFields.name: tunnel-config-origin-request-disable-chunked-encoding
requestBodyFields.description: Disables chunked transfer encoding. Useful if you are running a WSGI server.

requestBodyFields.name: tunnel-config-origin-request-http2origin
requestBodyFields.description: Attempt to connect to origin using HTTP2. Origin must be configured as https.

requestBodyFields.name: tunnel-config-origin-request-http-host-header
requestBodyFields.description: Sets the HTTP Host header on requests sent to the local service.

requestBodyFields.name: tunnel-config-origin-request-keep-alive-connections
requestBodyFields.description: Maximum number of idle keepalive connections between Tunnel and your origin. This does not restrict the total number of concurrent connections.

requestBodyFields.name: tunnel-config-origin-request-keep-alive-timeout
requestBodyFields.description: Timeout after which an idle keepalive connection can be discarded.

requestBodyFields.name: tunnel-config-origin-request-match-snito-host
requestBodyFields.description: Auto configure the Hostname on the origin server certificate.

requestBodyFields.name: tunnel-config-origin-request-no-happy-eyeballs
requestBodyFields.description: Disable the “happy eyeballs” algorithm for IPv4/IPv6 fallback if your local network has misconfigured one of the protocols.

requestBodyFields.name: tunnel-config-origin-request-no-tlsverify
requestBodyFields.description: Disables TLS verification of the certificate presented by your origin. Will allow any certificate from the origin to be accepted.

requestBodyFields.name: tunnel-config-origin-request-origin-server-name
requestBodyFields.description: Hostname that cloudflared should expect from your origin server certificate.

requestBodyFields.name: tunnel-config-origin-request-proxy-type
requestBodyFields.description: cloudflared starts a proxy server to translate HTTP traffic into TCP when proxying, for example, SSH or RDP. This configures what type of proxy will be started. Valid options are: "" for the regular proxy and "socks" for a SOCKS5 proxy.

requestBodyFields.name: tunnel-config-origin-request-tcp-keep-alive
requestBodyFields.description: The timeout after which a TCP keepalive packet is sent on a connection between Tunnel and the origin server.

requestBodyFields.name: tunnel-config-origin-request-tls-timeout
requestBodyFields.description: Timeout for completing a TLS handshake to your origin server, if you have chosen to connect Tunnel to an HTTPS server.

requestBodyFields.name: approval-groups
requestBodyFields.description: Administrators who can approve a temporary authentication request. Provide as a JSON array of objects or @path/to/file.json.

requestBodyFields.name: approval-required
requestBodyFields.description: Requires the user to request access from an administrator at the start of each session.

requestBodyFields.name: connection-rules-rdp-allowed-clipboard-local-to-remote-formats
requestBodyFields.description: Clipboard formats allowed when copying from local machine to remote RDP session.

requestBodyFields.name: connection-rules-rdp-allowed-clipboard-remote-to-local-formats
requestBodyFields.description: Clipboard formats allowed when copying from remote RDP session to local machine.

requestBodyFields.name: isolation-required
requestBodyFields.description: Require this application to be served in an isolated browser for users matching this policy. 'Client Web Isolation' must be on for the account in order to use this feature.

requestBodyFields.name: mfa-config-allowed-authenticators
requestBodyFields.description: Lists the MFA methods that users can authenticate with.

requestBodyFields.name: mfa-config-mfa-disabled
requestBodyFields.description: Indicates whether to disable MFA for this resource. This option is available at the application and policy level.

requestBodyFields.name: mfa-config-session-duration
requestBodyFields.description: Defines the duration of an MFA session. Must be in minutes (m) or hours (h). Minimum: 0m. Maximum: 720h (30 days). Examples:`5m` or `24h`.

requestBodyFields.name: purpose-justification-prompt
requestBodyFields.description: A custom message that will appear on the purpose justification screen.

requestBodyFields.name: purpose-justification-required
requestBodyFields.description: Require users to enter a justification when they log in to the application.

requestBodyFields.name: session-duration
requestBodyFields.description: The amount of time that tokens issued for the application will be valid. Must be in the format `300ms` or `2h45m`. Valid time units are: ns, us (or µs), ms, s, m, h.

requestBodyFields.name: decision
requestBodyFields.description: The action Access will take if a user matches this policy. Infrastructure application policies can only use the Allow action.

requestBodyFields.name: exclude
requestBodyFields.description: Rules evaluated with a NOT logical operator. To match the policy, a user cannot meet any of the Exclude rules. Provide as a JSON array of objects or @path/to/file.json.

requestBodyFields.name: include
requestBodyFields.description: Rules evaluated with an OR logical operator. A user needs to meet only one of the Include rules. Provide as a JSON array of objects or @path/to/file.json.

requestBodyFields.name: name
requestBodyFields.description: The name of the Access policy.

requestBodyFields.name: policy-resolution-account-id
requestBodyFields.description: The account ID used to resolve policy resources and identity for cross-account WARP authentication. The account must be trusted by the account that owns this policy.

requestBodyFields.name: require
requestBodyFields.description: Rules evaluated with an AND logical operator. To match the policy, a user must meet all of the Require rules. Provide as a JSON array of objects or @path/to/file.json.
